##### SUMMARY
If an environment value (of an env key) set on a task is a dict or a list then the actual env value may not be what's expected. This PR converts these values to a json to ensure consistency across shell plugins.

Fixes https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/60956

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
environment

##### OTHER
Using the following playbook as an example

```
---
- hosts: '2019'
  gather_facts: no
  vars:
    some_var: some_value
    bla:
      foo: bar
      aaa: '{{ some_var }}'
      zzz: baz
  tasks:
  - win_shell: $env:testvar
    environment:
      testvar: '{{ item }}'
    loop:
    - '{{ bla }}'
    - [ '{{ bla }}' ]

  - shell: env | grep testvar
    environment:
      testvar: '{{ item }}'
    loop:
    - '{{ bla }}'
    - [ '{{ bla }}' ]
    delegate_to: localhost
```

We can see that before PowerShell is completely useless as the raw object being sent to the host is an actual dict/list and .NET is not helpful in their ToString implementations. On Python it is slightly more useful but the values aren't fully JSON compliant with their single quotes instead of double quotes. With this PR now both platforms align with each other and the JSON being set as the env var in Python uses double quotes.

An alternative is to set the key inside an actual string like;

```
environment:
  testvar: '"{{ my_dict }}"'`
```

But this causes the env var to be `testvar="{"key": "value"}"` where the value is double quoted potentially causing more issues with parsing it.

I'm not sure if this should be a JSON transform, seems more like an error to me. Users should be able to `|to_json`  the value of an env var if that is what they really want.

Going by @bcoca's comments above and it looks like we would want to error out if the type is a sequence type instead of assuming the user wants JSON. The original issue is only a problem if we use this pattern;

```
- set_fact:
    json_str: '{{ my_dict | to_json }}'

- shell: env | grep testenv
  environment:
    testenv: '{{ json_str }}'
```

Ansible's magic eval of values here is causing the string `json_str` to be parsed as a dict as it starts with `{`. If you were to enable [DEFAULT_JINJA2_NATIVE](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/reference_appendices/config.html#default-jinja2-native) then the above work fine as the Ansible magic no longer applies. If you cannot enable that config option then omitting the set_fact altogether and using `to_json` in the env section is also an alternative:

```
- shell: env | grep testenv
  environment:
    testenv: '{{ my_dict | to_json }}'
```

Because there are options today I propose we change this PR to error out instead of converting to json is a sequence type is encountered. I'll talk about this at the public agenda a bit more.

issue_context.title: win_shell: environment variables propagated incorrectly
issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY
win_shell propagates environment variables incorrectly in some situations.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
win_shell

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
```
ansible 2.8.4
  config file = /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = [u'/root/.ansible/plugins/modules', u'/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/lib/python2.7/site-packages/ansible
  executable location = /usr/bin/ansible
  python version = 2.7.5 (default, Jun 20 2019, 20:27:34) [GCC 4.8.5 20150623 (Red Hat 4.8.5-36)]
```

##### CONFIGURATION
```
DEFAULT_GATHERING(/etc/ansible/ansible.cfg) = smart
DEFAULT_LOAD_CALLBACK_PLUGINS(/etc/ansible/ansible.cfg) = True
DEFAULT_STDOUT_CALLBACK(/etc/ansible/ansible.cfg) = yaml
INJECT_FACTS_AS_VARS(/etc/ansible/ansible.cfg) = False
```

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
Control node: CentOS 7
Target host: Windows 7

##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
Run the playbook below.

```yaml
- hosts: win
  gather_facts: no
  tasks:
  - set_fact:
      bla:
        foo: bar
        zzz: baz
  - set_fact:
      bla_string: '{{bla | to_json}}'
  - win_shell: $env:testvar
    register: out
    environment:
      testvar: '{{bla_string}}'
  - debug:
      var: out
```

##### EXPECTED RESULTS
out.stdout should show stringified JSON.

##### ACTUAL RESULTS
out.stdout shows "System.Collections.Hashtable"

```
PLAY [win] ***************************************************************************************************************************

TASK [set_fact] **********************************************************************************************************************
ok: [10.10.10.20]

TASK [set_fact] **********************************************************************************************************************
ok: [10.10.10.20]

TASK [win_shell] *********************************************************************************************************************
changed: [10.10.10.20]

TASK [debug] *************************************************************************************************************************
ok: [10.10.10.20] => 
  out:
    changed: true
    cmd: $env:testvar
    delta: '0:00:00.640625'
    end: '2019-08-20 03:42:18.428517'
    failed: false
    rc: 0
    start: '2019-08-20 03:42:17.787892'
    stderr: ''
    stderr_lines: []
    stdout: |-
      System.Collections.Hashtable
    stdout_lines:
    - System.Collections.Hashtable

PLAY RECAP ***************************************************************************************************************************
10.10.10.20                : ok=4    changed=1    unreachable=0    failed=0    skipped=0    rescued=0    ignored=0
```

This seems to be somehow connected to bla_string not being piped through any filters. If testvar is set to '{{bla | to_json}}' (i.e. skipping the intermediate set_fact), you get stringified JSON as expected. It also works correctly if testvar is set to '{{bla_string | string}}'. The problem is not related to set_fact itself, because in the real playbook where I discovered this, bla_string was a variable being passed to a role.

Ok, change `testvar: '{{bla_string}}'` to `testvar: '"{{bla_string}}"'`.
it was read in powershell as {} and converted to hashtable and not read as a string.

Thanks @rdicroce for the report, I've opened https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/61295 which should enable this to work but I've added it to the Ansible meeting agenda to discuss further as it is a slight behaviour change on the Python.

Ultimately what is happening is that internally the JSON string is being converted back to a dict and that is being passed to the remote host as is. The suggestion from @ShachafGoldstein will work for what you need but it will cause the env var to contain the `"` and `"` as well as your JSON string. You would have to manually strip those out before you can use it in your PowerShell script.

I did some further testing and 61295 probably won't be going ahead as is as it implies a user wants it to be a json string and not some other dict represetation.

In your case you have 2 options today;

1. Set `testvar: '{{ bla | to_json }}'` on the actual task itself and not use set_fact for that filter like.

```
- hosts: win
  gather_facts: no
  tasks:
  - set_fact:
      bla:
        foo: bar
        zzz: baz

  - win_shell: $env:testvar
    register: out
    environment:
      testvar: '{{bla | to_json}}'

  - debug:
      var: out
```

Doing this means means the actual value for `testvar` is interpreted only at the 1 place the `to_json` filter will force that to be a string for the 1 invocation.

2. The other option is to enable [DEFAULT_JINJA2_NATIVE](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/reference_appendices/config.html#default-jinja2-native) and make sure your installed Jinja2 version is >= 2.10 and run the playbook you currently have as is.

The reason why this is happening today is Ansible has historically tried to interpret vars through Python's `eval` function. This would result in a string that starts with `{` or `[` to be converted to an actual dict or list respectively.  Having `set_fact` set the var based on the `to_json` filter would result in a string like `{"foo": "bar", "zzz": "baz"}`. When Ansible goes to interepret `testvar: '{{ bla_string }}'` it will see the first char as `{` and "try" to be helpful and automatically convert it to a dict. This is "useful" in some situations due to historical Jinja2 behaviour but causes some of the confusion we see here. Having the default Jinja2 native types enabled means that it disables some of the Ansible magic and a string set as a fact will stay as a string.

Because the proper options today are either 1 or 2 I am going to close this issue. You can track the progress on 61295 but I am probably going to advocate a different direction in the Ansible meeting and won't help you with this use case.
